title: Felix and the Portrait
premise: Silas Amberdale, a taxi dispatcher who has spent a decade perfecting invisibility, receives two letters after the death of wealthy recluse Edvard Lune: one confessing to the unsolved murder of Lune's sister, one promising Silas a share of the inheritance. The letters pull Silas back to Amberdale House, where the portrait of the dead woman seems to watch, and where the family's lawyer, the housekeeper, and Lune's estranged son each have reasons to want the case to stay closed. As the trial of the confessed killer approaches, Silas discovers the confession was bought and the real killer is the person quietly managing the estate, forcing them to choose between exposing the truth outside the law or letting justice fail one last time. In the end, Silas trades their anonymity for testimony, secures the inheritance for the sister's forgotten charity, and finally claims a name for themselves in the town's record.
about_author: Jonah Yarrow is the pen name of a former court stenographer who spent eleven years transcribing small-town trials before turning to fiction. They write mysteries about people the legal system overlooks, and live quietly in a coastal town they refuse to name.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes, One Hand
chapters.summary: POV Silas. On a slow night shift, Silas receives twin letters from the recently dead Edvard Lune: a confession to his sister's murder, and a promise of inheritance if Silas 'finishes what the courts cannot.' The handwriting on both is identical, which is impossible, since the confession claims a second person wrote it. Beat: dread wrapped in curiosity.

chapters.title: The Night Everyone Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Silas, with flashback. Silas recalls the murder of Vivienne Lune fifteen years ago, a case Silas's own father was questioned in before his quiet disgrace. The town swore it was closed when a drifter was charged. Beat: personal stakes surface; the letters are not random.

chapters.title: Amberdale House Opens Its Mouth
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Silas visits the crumbling estate, met by lawyer Corwin Ashe, who is briskly cataloguing the inheritance. A portrait of Vivienne dominates the stairwell, its eyes repainted recently, the varnish still tacky. Beat: unease; the house is being erased and preserved at once.

chapters.title: The Housekeeper's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Housekeeper Maren Pike lets slip that Edvard spent his last months paying someone monthly, amounts matching the letters' postmarks. She warns Silas that the last person who asked questions left town. Beat: first threat, delivered politely.

chapters.title: A Son Returns
chapters.summary: POV alternating Silas and Tobias Lune. Edvard's estranged son Tobias arrives to contest the will, charming and brittle, insisting his father was senile and the letters meaningless. Silas notices Tobias flinches at the portrait. Beat: a suspect introduced, sympathy entangled with suspicion.

chapters.title: What the Confession Buys
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Silas tracks the confessed killer, dying drifter Ansel Rook, in a hospice upstate. Ansel admits he took money to confess, but can't remember who paid him, only 'a voice on a taxi radio.' Beat: the case bends toward Silas's own past.

chapters.title: Dispatch Logs and Dead Air
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Digging into the old taxi company archives, Silas finds a night of erased dispatch tapes from the murder, signed out by a dispatcher who never existed. The employee ID matches Silas's own father's badge number. Beat: the mystery turns intimate and painful.

chapters.title: The Portrait's Second Face
chapters.summary: POV Silas with Tobias. Under the repainted varnish, X-rays taken by a local restorer reveal Vivienne's portrait was painted over an earlier canvas: a half-finished self-portrait of the killer's hand holding a key. Beat: revelation; the evidence was hidden in plain sight for fifteen years.

chapters.title: Trial Date Set
chapters.summary: POV Silas and prosecutor Dana Voss. With Ansel's trial looming, Voss offers Silas immunity for testimony, but only for what Ansel says, not what Silas suspects. Corwin Ashe pressures the estate to settle before discovery. Beat: the clock starts; law and truth diverge.

chapters.title: Maren's Night Off
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Following Maren, Silas finds her burning papers behind the greenhouse: Edvard's private investigation into his sister's death, pages missing. Maren admits she was Edvard's accomplice in buying the confession, to protect someone she loves. Beat: loyalty as motive; an ally becomes ambiguous.

chapters.title: The Key in the Painting
chapters.summary: POV Silas. The key in the underpainting fits the estate's boathouse, where Silas finds Vivienne's hidden journals: she was documenting the family's fraudulent land dealings, and feared someone inside the house. Beat: the motive reframes; Vivienne becomes a person, not a victim.

chapters.title: Tobias's Alibi, Reassembled
chapters.summary: POV Tobias. Tobias's chapter reveals he was fourteen, sneaking back from a boarding school escape the night of the murder, and his father covered for him. He believes his own absence is the family's guilt. Beat: false confession of a different kind; grief misread as guilt.

chapters.title: Someone Reroutes the Night Shift
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Silas's cab assignments are manipulated; a fare to Amberdale House ends with brakes failing on the ridge road. Silas survives, realizing the killer knows the dispatch system from inside. Beat: danger becomes physical; the invisible watcher is now watching Silas.

chapters.title: The Dispatcher Who Never Was
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Cross-referencing payroll ghosts, Silas identifies the phantom dispatcher's paychecks, all cashed at a bank branch where Corwin Ashe was once manager. Beat: the lawyer enters the frame, but the proof is circumstantial.

chapters.title: Ansel's Last Ride
chapters.summary: POV Silas and Ansel. Ansel dies overnight, but not before dictating a memory: the voice on the radio that recruited him said 'Amberdale keeps its own accounts.' Silas tapes it on an old dispatcher recorder. Beat: a dying declaration, fragile and admissible only in conscience.

chapters.title: Corwin's Account
chapters.summary: POV Silas confronting Ashe. Cornered, Ashe confesses to the cover-up: he helped Vivienne's killer stage the scene and later brokered Ansel's confession, but claims he only 'kept the accounts' for the true killer, whom he refuses to name. Beat: partial truth; the web tightens around someone else.

chapters.title: The Portrait Watched Me Do It
chapters.summary: POV Maren. Maren's interlude reveals the truth she has carried: Edvard's brother, Aldous Lune, presumed dead abroad, returned secretly and killed Vivienne to silence her land-fraud evidence; Edvard spent his fortune hiding Aldous, then spent his last months trying to undo it. Beat: the confession letters explained; the real killer named.

chapters.title: Aldous Comes Home
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Aldous appears at the estate, living openly as a 'family friend,' and offers Silas the inheritance outright in exchange for the journals, the tape, and silence. The portrait of Vivienne is crated for removal that same hour. Beat: temptation priced exactly at Silas's price; climax approaches.

chapters.title: The Night Shift, Reversed
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Silas stages a final dispatch: luring Aldous to the boathouse with word that Vivienne's journals name an accomplice still alive. Aldous confesses on the open radio channel, the old dispatcher's recorder running, with Maren and Tobias listening. Beat: climax; the invisible medium becomes the trap.

chapters.title: Justice, Out of Hours
chapters.summary: POV Silas. The law falters: the recording's legality is doubtful and Ansel's trial collapses with his death. Silas chooses testimony anyway, handing Voss the journals, the underpainting evidence, and their father's cleared name. Aldous flees but is caught at the border with the estate key still in his coat. Beat: costly, imperfect justice.

chapters.title: The Reading of the Will
chapters.summary: POV Silas and Tobias. Edvard's true will, hidden in the portrait's frame backing, leaves the estate to Vivienne's chosen charity, with the house and a modest sum to Silas, 'for finishing the dispatch.' Tobias, freed from false guilt, offers Silas a role restoring the portrait. Beat: inheritance redefined as responsibility, not money.

chapters.title: Felix Signs the Log
chapters.summary: POV Silas. In the coda, Silas restores Vivienne's portrait, hangs it where the light finds it, and, for the first time, signs the town's record with a chosen name: Felix Amberdale. The final dispatch log entry reads 'case closed, driver remaining on shift.' Beat: identity claimed; invisibility surrendered willingly.
